judgeNotes.zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash: The road arrives fully rendered over a flat slab of ground at 10% and the trees spread as a scalloped, stamped-looking front rather than accumulating drawn strokes, reading more as a procedural fill than a brush-and-pen working order.

hills.painterNote: Cover everything outside the light hill polygons with many individual oak crowns (bigger toward the bottom) in blue-grey and navy glazes instead of a few green blobs, shape the light hills as diagonal bands with grass streaks, and add a bluer palette, because attempt 1 left too much bare green, too saturated and too yellow, against a target that is mostly dark blue-grey oak.

judgeNotes.zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash: A credible watercolor build — broad pale washes first, form-following mid-tone modeling on the hull, darks and rigging late, fine speckle detail in the final pass — with only the suspiciously flat, even-toned hull slab at 10% as a small tell.

sargent.painterNote: Hull as a dome with greyer warmer blue (umber/sienna) and lifted sheen arcs, pale sparse sky on warm paper instead of blue boxes, tapered strokes with ragged ends, connected teal water, ~300 varied strokes with dry-brush and dotted rigging, because a1 was a flat saturated blue rectangle with square-ended bands.

judgeNotes.zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash: A pen-and-wash sketcher would establish the village linework early; instead foliage dabs blanket the whole sheet, the houses surface only at 75% as flat white cut-out slabs with hard polygon edges, and every pen line, roof and window dumps in at the end — a masked reveal rather than a painter's order.

south-france.painterNote: Attempt 2: cover the sheet with dense layered green (mask the terrace and houses, then paint many overlapping individual trees with shadow crescents and glazes) because attempt 1 left most of the sheet pale cream with sparse blobs while the target is mostly dense olive green; also softer ink and pink-grey stone walls.
